removed.duration: Permanent zoning code amendment (not a fixed-term pause), prohibiting standalone data centers larger than 5,000 square feet citywide. removed.legal_basis: Zoning code amendment adopted by the Sandpoint City Council on 2026-09-16, prohibiting data centers exceeding 5,000 square feet as a land use (previously permitted, without a specific definition, in the city's Industrial Technology Park zoning district).
removed.trigger: Councilor Pam Duquette discovered that Sandpoint's Industrial zoning code specifically permitted data centers in the Industrial Technology Park district (roughly 19 parcels east of the airport) and sought to preemptively close that door before any developer applied, citing electricity and water demand; a concurrent state law (Idaho HB 895) newly requires closed-loop cooling for data centers statewide.
removed.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23 (permanent). Sandpoint's zoning code now prohibits standalone data centers larger than 5,000 square feet within city limits. City Planner Bill Dean and commissioners noted the size/land constraints of the city's only eligible industrial zone would have precluded a large ('hyperscale') facility from being built in the city regardless; the ban is aimed at foreclosing any use of the Industrial Technology Park district for a data center as that zone is redeveloped. No data center had been proposed in Sandpoint at any point in this process.
removed.affected_projects: None named; no data center had been proposed within Sandpoint city limits at any point in this process.
removed.outcome: City Council adopted a zoning amendment permanently prohibiting data centers over 5,000 square feet within city limits.

removed.duration: Proposed permanent zoning-code clarification (Bill 170) confirming that industrial-scale data centers are not a permitted use anywhere in Hawaii County (not a fixed-term pause). Introduced by Hamakua Councilmember Heather Kimball; the Council's Policy Committee on Planning, Land Use, and Economic Development voted unanimously on 2026-07-08 to forward it to the county's Windward and Leeward Planning Commissions for review. The Windward Planning Commission voted 4-0 on 2026-09-03 to defer action to its next meeting (2026-10-01); the Leeward Planning Commission's next meeting is 2026-10-15. Both commissions have until 2026-11-04 to forward a recommendation to the full Council (silence counts as a negative recommendation); no final Council vote had occurred as of 2026-09-23.
removed.legal_basis: Bill 170 (Hawaii County), introduced by Councilmember Heather Kimball; would add a zoning-code definition of 'data center' distinct from the existing, already-permitted 'data processing facility' definition, making explicit that data centers are excluded from the uses permitted under Hawaii County Code Section 25-4-4 (industrial-commercial mixed-use district). Not yet enacted.
removed.trigger: Councilmember Kimball cited industry statements of an intent to build roughly 3,000 U.S. data centers by decade's end, including 'in every state,' and sought to close a perceived zoning loophole (the 'campusing loophole,' i.e., splitting a large facility across adjacent parcels to evade review) before any developer files a permit application; Hawaii County's Planning Director stated he was not aware of any pending data center permit application, only informal inquiries. More than 40 pieces of testimony were submitted, mostly in favor, citing water and electricity costs, noise, and grid-capacity concerns on an isolated island system.
removed.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23. Bill 170 would amend Hawaii County's zoning code to distinguish 'data centers' (industrial-scale AI/computing facilities) from already-permitted 'data processing facilities,' making explicit that data centers are not a permitted use anywhere in the county absent a further state or county land-use change; existing university (UH Hilo) and telecom (Hawaiian Telcom, Kawaihae) data facilities are exempted/grandfathered. The Council committee forwarded the bill unanimously on 2026-07-08 for planning-commission review. The Windward Planning Commission deferred action 4-0 on 2026-09-03 to its 2026-10-01 meeting; the Leeward Planning Commission's next hearing is 2026-10-15; both commissions must report to the full Council by 2026-11-04. County Planning Director Jeff Darrow has instead proposed allowing data centers under 10,000 sq ft (or an electricity-use threshold) by right in the general industrial district, with larger facilities requiring a discretionary use permit, rather than an outright ban -- an alternative the commissions are weighing alongside Kimball's bill.
removed.affected_projects: None named; Hawaii County's Planning Director stated no data center permit application has been filed, only informal developer inquiries.
removed.outcome: County Council committee forwarded a bill to clarify/confirm that data centers are not a permitted zoning use; still under Planning Commission review as of this pass, with a Council decision not expected before November 2026.

removed.notes: This is a proposed PERMANENT zoning clarification/prohibition, not a fixed-term pause; recorded as 'pending' consistent with how this inventory already treats other not-yet-adopted permanent prohibition proposals (e.g., the Perris, CA candidate in work/answers/full/CA.json). The bill's own text frames it as confirming an existing default prohibition (unlisted uses are unpermitted under County Code) rather than creating a new one, so it is a borderline case; it is included because press coverage, testimony, and the coordinating council office all frame it squarely as the county's answer to the national data-center-moratorium wave, and it is working through a live legislative process with a defined near-term timeline (commissions report to Council by 2026-11-04). No other Hawaii jurisdiction (Honolulu, Maui, Kauai) or sector (battery storage, solar, wind, cryptocurrency mining) turned up any enacted or proposed moratorium in this pass; see final report for queries run.

removed.duration: Proposed permanent citywide prohibition on data centers as a primary land use in any zoning category (not a fixed-term pause). The Planning and Zoning Commission narrowly endorsed the ban proposal 4-3 (with one abstention counted as an affirmative vote under the city charter) at its March 25, 2026 meeting, alongside a competing, staff-recommended conditional-use-permit (CUP) alternative. The City Council was originally scheduled to vote May 5, 2026, but on 2026-05-05 postponed the item indefinitely 'until later this year' for a 'comprehensive evaluation'; no new hearing or vote date had been set as of 2026-09-23.
removed.legal_basis: Draft zoning code text amendment (two competing versions: an outright prohibition and a conditional-use-permit requirement) recommended for Council consideration by the Flagstaff Planning and Zoning Commission on 2026-03-25; no ordinance number exists because neither version has been adopted by the City Council.
removed.trigger: City staff identified the absence of any zoning-code definition or regulation of data centers as a 'hole' to be addressed proactively; public concern (including a March 2026 NAU panel on data centers on Southwest Native lands, and a separate contested data center proposal north of Flagstaff near Page) focused on electricity and water demand and noise, even though no developer has yet proposed building a data center within Flagstaff city limits.
removed.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23. Flagstaff's zoning code does not currently mention or regulate data centers. City staff proposed a conditional-use-permit process; the Planning and Zoning Commission instead narrowly endorsed (4-3, one abstention counted affirmative) a competing draft that would prohibit data centers outright as a primary use in any zoning category, at its March 25, 2026 meeting. The City Council, not bound by the commission's recommendation, twice postponed considering either version (from April 7 to May 5, then indefinitely on 2026-05-05), with the zoning code manager citing insufficient public engagement on the ban-focused draft and stating the item would return to the Planning and Zoning Commission and to Council 'later this year' after a 'comprehensive evaluation.' No developer has proposed building a data center within Flagstaff city limits as of this pass; a separate, unrelated data center proposal near Page (north of Flagstaff, outside city jurisdiction) has drawn local political controversy.
removed.affected_projects: None named; city officials repeatedly stated no developer has proposed a data center within Flagstaff city limits, and note the city currently has no parcels large enough to accommodate a 'hyperscale' facility.
removed.outcome: Planning and Zoning Commission recommended a citywide data center ban (March 2026); City Council indefinitely postponed a decision between that ban and a staff-recommended conditional-use-permit alternative (May 2026); no Council vote has occurred as of this pass.
